alina: Heads-up — hit a reproducibility issue between Python SDK + TS SDK for generate calls. Observed that when callers omit temperature, TS omits the field (server default 0.7), but Python seems to send temperature=0.0 which makes outputs much more deterministic. Is this a known mismatch?

sam: Which endpoint/version are you hitting? v1/generate or the new /api/v1/models/:id/generate?

alina: v1/generate on prod. Quick reproduction:
```
# python (redwood-sdk v2.1.0)
client.generate(model="gpt-xyz", input="hi")
# network payload contains: { "temperature": 0.0 }

# typescript (redwood-js v3.0.2)
client.generate({ model: 'gpt-xyz', input: 'hi' })
# network payload: no temperature field
```
Result: TS requests use server default 0.7, py requests use 0.0.

maria: Thanks, this rings a bell. We introduced a signature change in python v2.1.0: `def generate(..., temperature: float = 0.0)` instead of `Optional[float] = None`. That default leaks into the serialized body when omitted. TS correctly leaves it undefined so the server default applies. This is a bug — thanks for catching it.

jon: Server accepts both "temperature" and legacy "temp" keys and applies default 0.7 if the field is absent. If SDK explicitly sends 0.0 we treat it as a real value. We can consider treating 0.0 == omitted for a short window, but that seems risky.

maria: Plan: revert python default to None in a 2.1.1 patch so omission serializes nothing. Add a deprecation warning if callers pass temperature=0.0 explicitly? (we should NOT silently change semantics if a user intentionally set 0.0). I'll open PR and add unit tests for serialization. PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python-sdk/pull/4523 (WIP)

alina: Sounds good. Can we also add an integration test that asserts server receives no temperature key when the arg is omitted? Caught this in a product test — pretty nasty to debug.

sam: +1 on integration test. @eng-platform can you run an e2e against canary when PR is ready? We should also add a regression test comparing Python vs TS payloads.

jon: I can add a server-side guard in the compatibility layer to accept both behaviors for one release window and log telemetry if temperature==0.0 and client is python-sdk@2.1.0.

ci-bot: CI for PR #4523: running tests -> found missing unit test for `test_generate_serializes_temperature`. Failing currently.

maria: Thanks @ci-bot — I'll add the test. Also will include a changelog note and a short blurb in the SDK migration guide: "If you relied on implicit default 0.0 from python v2.1.0, you will see different outputs after 2.1.1. Explicit 0.0 remains supported." 

alina: Great, thanks. Ping me when PR is ready and I'll smoke-test some workflows.

maria: will do — aiming to ship patch today. cc @sam @jon
